title: Accessibility of the Ind fibration over a presheaf category
statement: Use universes, accessibility, compactness and presentability from [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], coherent functors and spaces from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and Cartesian fibrations from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Let $A$ be a small infinity category and $\lambda$ an infinite regular cardinal in the smaller universe. Let $F_0:A\to\operatorname{Cat}^{\mathrm{rex}(\lambda)}_\infty$ be a coherent functor to small infinity categories admitting $\lambda$-small colimits, with arrows preserving those colimits. For such a category $C$, write $\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(C)\subseteq\operatorname{Fun}(C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$ for the full subcategory of small $\lambda$-filtered colimits of representables, where $\mathcal S$ is the infinity category of small spaces. For $f:a\to a'$ let $H(f^{\mathrm{op}})$ be the right adjoint of the $\lambda$-filtered-colimit-preserving extension of $F_0(f)$ to Ind categories, and put $H(a)=\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda(F_0(a))$. This gives a coherent functor $H:A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$. Put $\mathcal P(A)=\operatorname{Fun}(A^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$ and let $y:A\to\mathcal P(A)$ be Yoneda. There exists a coherent extension $\widehat H:\mathcal P(A)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ of $H$ along $y^{\mathrm{op}}$ taking all small colimit cocones in $\mathcal P(A)$ to limit cones. It is unique up to natural equivalence with its extension data. More explicitly, for $X\in\mathcal P(A)$ let $A_{/X}$ be the category with objects $(a,y(a)\to X)$ and coherent triangles as morphisms, formed as the category of elements of the small-space-valued presheaf $X$; it is small up to equivalence. Then the canonical extension cone gives a natural equivalence $\widehat H(X)\simeq\lim_{(a,y(a)\to X)\in A_{/X}^{\mathrm{op}}}H(a)$. For a Cartesian fibration $q:\widehat{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal P(A)$ classified by $\widehat H$, the total infinity category $\widehat{\mathcal E}$ is accessible and $q$ is accessible, meaning that it preserves small $\mu$-filtered colimits for some infinite regular cardinal $\mu$. All these size assertions are relative to the smaller universe; the total category and presheaf category are allowed to be large in it and are formed in a containing universe. Here $L:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ is left adjoint to $R:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C$ when there is an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(Lx,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(x,Ry)$ natural coherently in $x,y$, with the corresponding coherent unit and counit satisfying the triangle identities.

source.place: Definition 10.4 and Proposition 10.5, including its proof via Corollary 9.17 and Lemma 10.6. The extension and its category-of-elements formula are the dual presheaf universal property (HTT Theorem 5.1.5.6); HTT Proposition 5.5.7.6 ensures the limits in the uniform right-adjoint category are underlying categorical limits. Read online; archival copies WANTED in report.md. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text: For each $a\in A$, apply [lem-coef-ind-kappa-presentability] to $F_0(a)$. Because $F_0(a)$ is small and admits all $\lambda$-small colimits, its $\operatorname{Ind}_\lambda$ category is presentable, generated by the representables under $\lambda$-filtered colimits, and the representables are $\lambda$-compact. For an arrow $f:a\to a'$, compose the $\lambda$-small-colimit-preserving functor $F_0(f)$ with the Yoneda embedding of $F_0(a')$, which preserves these colimits by [lem-coef-ind-kappa-presentability]. Its extension preserves all small colimits by the final clause of [lem-coef-ind-kappa-extension]; since source and target Ind categories are presentable, [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] supplies the right adjoint used to define $H(f^{\mathrm{op}})$. The coherent functoriality of these Ind constructions, including the right-adjoint variance and all higher simplices for an arbitrary infinite regular cardinal, is supplied by [lem-coef-ind-right-adjoint-coherent]. Thus the displayed $H:A^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ is well-defined with the stated fibers and transports.

source.place: Definition 10.4 and the construction preceding Proposition 10.5

proof.text: The containing-universe category $\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ admits all working-universe small limits by [lem-coef-cat-infinity-colimits-cartesian-closure], so its opposite admits the colimits needed for [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion]. Apply the free-cocompletion equivalence [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-free-cocompletion] after passing to opposites: regard $H$ as a functor $A\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty^{\mathrm{op}}$, extend it uniquely to a small-colimit-preserving functor $\mathcal P(A)\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty^{\mathrm{op}}$, and take opposites. The result is a coherent functor $\widehat H:\mathcal P(A)^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Cat}_\infty$ whose restriction along $y^{\mathrm{op}}$ is $H$. Since the extension preserves colimits before taking opposites, it takes every small colimit cocone in $\mathcal P(A)$ to a limit cone. The same restriction equivalence gives the asserted uniqueness up to natural equivalence, including its coherent extension data.

source.place: Definition 10.4; dual presheaf universal property (HTT Theorem 5.1.5.6)

proof.text: For $X\in\mathcal P(A)$, use the canonical representable-slice cocone supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-representable-slice-density]. Its indexing quasicategory is the category of elements $A_{/X}$ with vertices $(a,y(a)\to X)$, is small up to equivalence, and its cocone of representables is colimiting. Applying the colimit-to-limit extension from step 2 to that cocone gives, naturally in $X$, $\widehat H(X)\simeq\lim_{(a,y(a)\to X)\in A_{/X}^{\mathrm{op}}}H(a)$. The construction retains the coherent triangles and higher homotopies because the cited slice statement is a statement about the canonical coherent cocone, not merely its homotopy category.

Form the cocartesian fibration $p:E\to A$ classified by $F_0$ using [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening]. Its smallness convention makes $E$ and the relative cone $D=E_A^{\triangleleft}$ small. The classification node [lem-coef-ghn-ind-presheaf-cartesian-realization] identifies the desired Cartesian fibration with restriction from the full relative-cone presheaf subcategory defined by conditions (i) and (ii).

Condition (ii) of [lem-coef-ghn-ind-presheaf-cartesian-realization] is exactly that $E_a^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S_{/X(a)}$ take $\lambda$-small colimits in $E_a$ to limits in the slice. The source has the required limits by the hypothesis on $F_0(a)$. Spaces have small limits by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]; applying [lem-coef-infinity-coslice-colimit-formula] to $\mathcal S^{\mathrm{op}}$ shows that its slices have small limits as well. Thus [lem-coef-infinity-limits-products-pullbacks] applies to this functor: it suffices to test fiber pushouts and coproducts indexed by sets of cardinality less than $\lambda$, including the empty one. The relative limit interpretation, including the common target $X(a)$, is part of the cited GHN statement.

source.place: Proposition 9.16 proof, slice interpretation of the double-cone limit, and Proposition 10.5 proof, reduction to pushouts and small coproducts; existing dual coslice formula supplies slice completeness.

proof.text: Choose one representative of each such fiber diagram and cocartesian-edge square. By [lem-coef-ind-presheaf-small-locality-generators] these representatives give a small set $S_0$ of maps $s_r:\operatorname{colim}_{b\in B}y_D(r(b))\to y_D(r(\infty))$ whose local objects are exactly the relative-cone presheaves. The comparison for each $s_r$ is the map $\phi(r(\infty))\to\lim_{b\in B^{\mathrm{op}}}\phi(r(b))$, by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-evaluation] and [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits].

source.place: Proposition 10.5 proof, Lemma 10.6 and Yoneda locality test

proof.text: The ambient presheaf category is presentable by [lem-coef-infinity-presheaf-presentability]. The small-localization clause of [lem-coef-presentable-infinity-adjoints] supplies a reflector $L$ with inclusion $i$, and local colimits are $L$ of ambient colimits. For $s\in S_0$, the adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Map}(Ls,Z)$ with $\operatorname{Map}(s,iZ)$, an equivalence for every local $Z$; Yoneda therefore makes $Ls$ an equivalence. Conversely the same adjunction makes every local $Z$ local for every map inverted by $L$. Both hypotheses of [lem-coef-infinity-reflector-accessibility] hold, so the local category and $iL$ are accessible.

Choose an infinite regular $\mu$ for which $iL$ preserves $\mu$-filtered colimits. For a $\mu$-filtered diagram $Z$ of local objects, $i\operatorname{colim}Z\simeq iL\operatorname{colim}iZ\simeq\operatorname{colim}iLiZ\simeq\operatorname{colim}iZ$, so $i$ is accessible. Restriction $j^*:\mathcal P(D)\to\mathcal P(A)$ preserves colimits pointwise by [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]; therefore the classified projection is accessible and the total category is accessible.

Use the opposite of the straightening equivalence [lem-coef-cocartesian-straightening] in a containing universe to unstraighten $\widehat H$ as a Cartesian fibration $q:\widehat{\mathcal E}\to\mathcal P(A)$. The classification identifies its fiber over $X$ with $\widehat H(X)$ and its restriction maps with the prescribed right-adjoint transports. The accessible-total-category and accessible-projection conclusion of steps 4–8 is invariant under this straightening/unstraightening equivalence, so $\widehat{\mathcal E}$ is accessible and $q$ preserves small $\mu$-filtered colimits for some infinite regular $\mu$, as required.
